scope: Source-reviewed practical outlines; partial coverage is explicit. No invented timestamps or automatic skill certification.

hingePractice.purpose: Rehearse the hip hinge and bracing used to prepare a two-hand kettlebell deadlift.
setup: Begin without external load, feet about shoulder width. Place hands in the hip folds.
steps: Push the hips back with weight through the heels.
Stand tall, straighten the legs and squeeze the glutes.
Repeat the controlled hinge while keeping the trunk aligned.
bracing: Keep the rib cage down, glutes engaged and shoulders away from the ears.
mistakes: If the knees drive forward instead of the hips moving back, return to the unloaded setup.

evidence.quote: without the weight normally this is just done

deadlift.purpose: Develop a controlled loaded hinge before learning a ballistic swing.
setup: Place the bell between the insteps. Set a manageable familiar load and a shoulder-width stance.
steps: Hinge back and reach down the inside of the legs.
Stand tall with controlled leg drive and glute engagement.
Return the bell to the ground with the same controlled hinge.
bracing: Maintain trunk alignment and drive the rib cage down rather than arching the back.
mistakes: Do not substitute a squat or shoulder lift for the hip hinge. Rehearse unloaded if position is inconsistent.

evidence.quote: all other exercises are built off of this structure

swing.purpose: Practice hip-driven front-to-back ballistic movement using the familiar deadlift foundation.
setup: Review the two-hand deadlift first. Stand a small step behind the bell, with a familiar stance and grip.
steps: Hinge back, take the bell with both hands and hike it behind you.
Drive through the legs and hips to stand; let that drive move the bell.
Hinge on the return. Park the bell under control and stand up after setting it down.
bracing: Keep the trunk aligned, glutes engaged at the top and shoulders away from the ears.
mistakes: Do not raise the bell by lifting with the shoulders. If alignment breaks down, stop and return to hinge practice.

evidence.quote: we are not lifting the weight with our shoulders

squat.purpose: Practice the goblet squat pattern with the load held in front of the body.
setup: Pick up the bell with control, heavy part uppermost. Hold it in front with elbows close.
steps: Descend under control with elbows tracking inside the knees.
Use the counterbalance to keep the trunk tall within a comfortable range.
Stand all the way up with straight legs and glute engagement. Set down with control.
bracing: Keep the bell supported by your grip rather than resting it on the body.
mistakes: Do not let the knees collapse inward. Keep the movement controlled rather than forcing depth.

evidence.quote: elbows track inside the knee

press.purpose: Press from a stable single-arm rack while the rest of the body provides support.
setup: Use two hands to establish a secure rack: flat wrist, vertical forearm and thumb near collarbone height.
steps: Stand with controlled leg and glute tension.
Open the shoulder and press to a familiar overhead lockout.
Pull down into the same rack position; use both hands for a controlled set-down.
bracing: Keep the glutes and abdominal wall engaged. Avoid lifting the rib cage to finish the press.
mistakes: If the bell drifts in front and you lean back, review rack, trunk tension and overhead position.

evidence.quote: make your body the bench

clean.purpose: Move the bell into a controlled rack using hip drive rather than an arm curl.
setup: Begin by using both hands to establish the rack. Check a flat wrist and the handle lying diagonally in the hand.
steps: Keep the elbow close to the hip as the bell moves back; turn the thumb back at the bottom.
Use the hips to stand and guide the bell back into the rack.
Pause and adjust the rack when needed. Use two hands to set down safely.
bracing: Maintain an aligned trunk and glute engagement at the catch.
mistakes: A bent wrist, elbow drifting out or hard forearm impact is a reason to stop and review the rack drill.

evidence.quote: flat wrist is key to your catch

row.purpose: Practice pulling while the torso resists rotation.
setup: Use a familiar, stable hinge. The lesson teaches unsupported rows after prior swing/clean practice.
steps: Hold the hinge with the lat engaged.
Draw the hand toward the space between the lower ribs and hip.
Straighten the arm on the return while keeping the body from twisting.
bracing: The source demonstrates inhaling on the lower/easier phase and exhaling on the pull. Maintain core tension.
mistakes: Do not rotate the trunk or move the head to complete a rep. Use a position your back can support.

evidence.quote: we are fighting that rotation

cast.purpose: Practice a two-hand path around the head as a shield-cast foundation.
setup: Use a familiar light club and the reviewed two-hand setup, with feet pointing forward.
steps: Guide the top hand past the opposite ear.
Allow the club to swing from side to side behind the body.
Keep the thumb path low toward the neckline rather than holding the hands high.
mistakes: Do not force the shoulder range or strike the body. The short lesson does not provide a complete breathing sequence.

evidence.quote: our top hand is going to go past our opposite ear

circles.purpose: Practice two-hand lateral circles; inside and outside are different directions.
setup: Set the club between the feet. Pick it up to order with the top arm near a right angle and elbow close to the body.
steps: For an inside circle, move the top hand toward the body center line.
Rotate, push, swing with straight elbows, pull and catch in order.
Return to center and stand tall. Change the high hand to train the other side.
bracing: Keep both feet planted while the hips and upper body turn.
mistakes: Bent elbows or shrugging as grip tires mean stop and rest; do not chase speed or failure.

evidence.quote: push tip swing pull catch

snatch.coverage: partial: breakdown outline, not a complete first-snatch lesson
snatch.purpose: Build a familiar overhead ballistic pattern from established clean-and-press skills.
setup: Start with controlled swing, clean and overhead skills. Review the flat-wrist overhead endpoint before linking the movement.
steps: The lesson breaks the skill into clean-and-press up / snatch down and snatch up / clean-and-press down.
Rehearse those reviewed parts before joining a complete snatch.
At the top, keep the bell supported in the hand rather than crashing over it.
bracing: The lesson demonstrates a double-exhale pattern; it also notes other breathing approaches.
mistakes: If the bell impacts the forearm or wrist position/control is lost, stop and return to the breakdown lesson.

evidence.quote: the kettlebell is not going over the top of our hand

doublePress.coverage: partial: combination outline; separate double-clean technique remains required
doublePress.purpose: Combine a familiar double clean and overhead press while maintaining trunk tension.
setup: Use a confirmed matched pair and familiar double-clean/rack technique. Leave room for both bells.
steps: Hike and clean the bells into a secure rack without crushing the hands.
Maintain body tension and press to the familiar overhead position.
Return fully to the rack before repeating the clean.
bracing: Keep the glutes engaged and rib cage controlled through the press and return.
mistakes: Do not let the bells force a bent wrist, unstable rack or backward lean. Review the separate double-clean/press lessons first.

evidence.quote: go back watch our double kettlebell clean video

doubleSquat.purpose: Practice a loaded squat from a familiar double rack.
setup: Use a manageable matched pair and a stable double rack. Stance must accommodate both bells and your frame.
steps: Maintain the rack while descending under control.
Track the elbows toward the insides of the knees and keep the chest supported.
Stand tall and squeeze the glutes; set down through the familiar double-clean technique.
bracing: Maintain a stable trunk and secure wrist position.
mistakes: Do not let the rack collapse or the bells crush the hands. The source teaches separate skills before combining them.

evidence.quote: elbows will track inside the knees

getupFloor.purpose: Practice the floor press and safe setup/return at the base of a get-up.
setup: Use the other hand to assist bringing the bell into position. Bend the same-side leg and place the free arm out around 45 degrees.
steps: Keep the forearm vertical with the elbow supported on the floor.
Press over the chest line rather than drifting toward the face.
Lower the elbow to the floor. Use the other hand to help roll the bell safely to the side.
bracing: Maintain a controlled wrist and forearm instead of letting the bell rest on the torso.
mistakes: Do not drop the bell away from the body or force a heavy one-hand setup/return.

evidence.quote: same side same leg

getupElbow.purpose: Link the floor press, roll and elbow support as a get-up breakdown.
setup: Use the familiar floor-press setup with the free hand out around 45 degrees.
steps: Press over the chest line.
Roll to the side and drive up onto the supporting elbow.
Reverse through the shoulders to the floor before lowering the press.
bracing: Maintain the overhead support line and keep the top knee from collapsing inward.
mistakes: Avoid repeatedly relocating the supporting hand; move the body through the controlled return.

evidence.quote: press roll elbow

getupHand.purpose: Progress from elbow support to a stable supporting hand.
setup: Use the established floor-press/elbow setup with a flat kettlebell wrist and the free hand around 45 degrees out.
steps: Press, roll, rise to the elbow, then press to the supporting hand.
Straighten the supporting elbow and create space between shoulder and ear.
Return hand → elbow → shoulders under control, then lower the press and assist the bell down.
bracing: Drive the supporting shoulder down and stabilize rather than shrugging toward the ear.
mistakes: Do not walk the hand around between transitions or let the loaded elbow soften.

evidence.quote: press roll elbow hand

getupHipPass.purpose: Practice the lower get-up transition through the hip/knee pass, without the final stand.
setup: Begin with the familiar floor setup, same-side bent leg and the free hand set around 45 degrees out.
steps: Press, roll, rise to elbow and then hand support.
Lift the hip and bring the knee back toward the line of the supporting hand.
Orient upright, then reverse through hand support and the controlled floor return.
bracing: Maintain the overhead elbow lock and flat supporting hand through the transition.
mistakes: If hand/knee placement is too shallow, return to the supported breakdown rather than forcing a stand.

evidence.quote: without the stand up at the top

getup.coverage: partial: programming goal, not a complete technique lesson
getup.purpose: Develop controlled alternating single get-ups under a total-time goal.
setup: Use a familiar complete get-up and the established floor/elbow/hand/hip skills on both sides.
mistakes: The time goal is not permission to rush a transition. Full step-by-step stand/lunge instruction still needs a dedicated review.

evidence.quote: three minutes four minutes five minutes six minutes seven minutes eight minutes nine minutes to get to our goal of 10 minutes

clubInside.purpose: Develop controlled rotation toward the body center line with one arm.
setup: Review the two-hand pattern first. Begin in order with the elbow close to the body and feet pointing forward.
steps: Load the same-side leg and rotate toward the center line.
Push, swing, pull and catch, then return to center and stand tall.
Practice equally with the other hand; remove the support hand only after a controlled two-hand foundation.
mistakes: Do not swing around the legs or allow the feet to drift. Stop before grip changes the path.

evidence.quote: inside means your top hand moves towards your Center Line

clubOutside.purpose: Develop the corresponding rotation away from the body center line.
setup: Use the familiar two-hand outside pattern and a controlled order position before removing support.
steps: Move away from the center line, using the opposite leg to start the motion.
Push, swing with controlled straight-arm extension, pull and catch with elbow toward hip.
Return to center and stand tall. Match both sides and the inside pattern.
mistakes: Do not bend the swinging elbow or hike the shoulder as the load crosses the bottom.

evidence.quote: push swing pull catch

clubShield.purpose: Build a single-arm shield cast from a substantial two-hand foundation.
setup: Review the two-hand cast first. Start and finish in order, elbow close to the body.
steps: Rotate the opposite shoulder toward the hand.
Guide the hand past the opposite ear, push behind the head, then pull over.
Catch in order. Keep the same cues while gradually removing the bottom-hand support.
mistakes: Do not skip the two-hand foundation or change the catch position to chase reps.

evidence.quote: rotate push pull catch

clubInsidePendulum.purpose: Practice a rotating clean toward the center line.
setup: Start in order with a familiar light club. Rehearse the movement with two hands first.
steps: Rotate from the legs toward the center line.
Push and swing down, allowing the chest to rotate toward the club.
Stand up, pull the elbow to the body and catch back in order.
mistakes: Keep the feet planted. Remove bottom-hand support only while retaining the full controlled rotation.

evidence.quote: Inside means moving towards our center line

clubOutsidePendulum.purpose: Practice the corresponding rotating clean away from the center line.
setup: Begin in order with the elbow near the hip. Review the two-hand outside pendulum before single-arm practice.
steps: Load the opposite leg and rotate away from center.
Push, swing with the arm extended, then drive with the hips.
Pull, catch in order and return to center; practice both sides.
mistakes: Do not lose rotation at the bottom when the support hand comes away.

evidence.quote: outside opposite leg loads

clubFrontPullover.purpose: Isolate the familiar straight-back/straight-forward pullover before adding rotation.
setup: Use a familiar light club in order with a stable stance.
steps: Guide the hand straight back, allowing the thumb path down toward the shirt.
Drive through the tricep and pull the club forward.
Return the elbow toward the hip and catch in order; match both arms.
bracing: Keep glutes engaged and resist the rib cage lifting as the club moves back.
mistakes: Do not hold the hand excessively high or force shoulder range.

evidence.quote: forward pullover straight back thumb touches shirt straight forward

clubOutsidePullover.purpose: Add an outside shoulder orientation to the familiar pullover.
setup: Build from the front-to-back pullover and a controlled order position.
steps: Rotate the hand away from the center line and guide it past the same-side ear.
Move back, then extend and pull over under control.
Return the elbow toward the hip and to the front before changing hands.
bracing: Resist lifting the rib cage; maintain glute and trunk tension.
mistakes: Do not confuse the same-side ear path with the opposite-ear shield cast.

evidence.quote: we go past our same side ear

clubInsidePullover.purpose: Practice a controlled inside pullover using the three-count breakdown.
setup: Build from familiar front/outside pullovers. Keep the feet planted and use a light familiar club.
steps: Rotate inward toward the body center line, passing the same-side ear.
Use the three-count breakdown to practice the low thumb path and controlled rotation.
Pull over, stop and demonstrate control in order before the next rep.
bracing: Use the legs/hips while keeping the feet in place; do not try to force the shoulder alone.
mistakes: Do not skip the deliberate counts or rush the catch to accumulate volume.

evidence.quote: stop demonstrate control

pushup.coverage: partial: clean standard/programming, not a full technique setup
pushup.purpose: Develop clean push-up volume using a conservative existing baseline.
setup: Review a push-up position you can keep aligned with the core engaged. The reviewed lesson is primarily about programming.
steps: Perform only clean repetitions within your configured submaximal prescription.
Stop the set when the stable trunk line is lost.
Keep the same prescribed reps while the volume cycle adds rounds.
bracing: Maintain core engagement rather than allowing the back to sway.
mistakes: Do not count poor repetitions toward the baseline or perform a new maximum test each workout. Detailed hand-placement instruction is not covered here.

evidence.quote: core engaged the whole time no back sway

hipDropTwoHand.purpose: Practice a small ground-transition component used in get-ups.
setup: Start standing, get down under control, then arrange flat hands and feet in a square with knees close to wrists.
steps: Lift the knees only a little off the floor.
Use quiet step-step transitions to lower the hip and thigh to the floor.
Return through center and change sides. Finish by standing up under control.
bracing: Exhale on the hip touch and inhale in the middle. Keep the supporting shoulder controlled.
mistakes: Avoid jumping, bucking the hips or letting feet creep away from the hands.

evidence.quote: the breath pattern is exhale

hipDropSingleHand.purpose: Progress the familiar two-hand hip drop by removing one supporting hand.
setup: Use the same square hand/foot setup and two-hand foundation.
steps: Step-step into the hip drop and lower the hip/thigh to the floor.
Lift the free hand toward a reading position, elbow toward the belly.
Replace the hand in its original spot and return through center to the other side. Finish standing.
bracing: Exhale as the hip touches, inhale in the middle and keep the supporting shoulder away from the ear.
mistakes: Do not let the base shoulder collapse or hand/foot placement drift farther away each rep.

evidence.quote: read the book elbow to belly button

bearSquat.purpose: Use moving quadruped practice to explore the kneeling-to-straight-leg range.
setup: Find hand distance from a comfortable kneeling/child position; use a knee pad if needed.
steps: Move toward the down-dog-like position with hands and feet staying in place.
Bend the knees back toward their original floor target.
Straighten again through controlled range, then return to kneeling at the end.
bracing: Keep the abdominal wall engaged and rib cage down; the source asks for attention to breathing, not a fixed breath count.
mistakes: Do not bend the elbows or let the setup creep across the floor. Do not force a range you cannot control.

evidence.quote: our goal is to keep the center of our chest in space

carry.purpose: Carry a unilateral load while maintaining posture.

front.purpose: Practice the existing two-hand front-swing pattern.
